newsitem.title: USA: NEORX, J&J UNIT STRIKE DEAL ON AVICIDIN.
newsitem.headline: NEORX, J&J UNIT STRIKE DEAL ON AVICIDIN.

text.p: NeoRx Corp said Tuesday it reached a deal with Janssen Pharmaceutica N.V., a subsidiary of Johnson & Johnson, for the development, manufacture and distribution of its Avicidin cancer therapy product.
Under the agreement, NeoRx receives $10 million upfront, of which half is in the form of an equity purchase. It may receive up to $50 million more in milestone payments.
NeoRx was up 15/16 at 5-3/8 early Tuesday afternoon. Johnson & Johnson dipped 3/16 to 58-3/16.

Janssen Pharmaceutica, of Beerse, Belgium, assumes responsibility for registration and commercialization of the product and will fund about 95 percent of the remaining costs for product development and clinical trials, NeoRx said.
Johnson & Johnson receives a worldwide exclusive license to market Avicidin, with undisclosed royalties going to NeoRx.

Johnson & Johnson also secures the right of first negotiation to subsequent oncology products based on NeoRx's Pretarget technology for delivering radiation therapy to tumor cells while minimizing exposure to normal tissue.

In early trials the technology has allowed physicians to deliver radiation therapy at five times the normal dosage to patients who have failed standard treatments. Avicidin is in Phase I/II clinical trials for solid tumors in the lung, colon, breast and prostate.

As part of the deal Johnson & Johnson Development Corp will buy $5 million of NeoRx convertible preferred stock that will convert automatically to common if the average share price of NeoRx equals or exceeds $6 a share in any 15-day period over the next year.
Otherwise the stock converts to common at the closing price August 8, 1998.
